primitives.name: Incremental Factor Graph Localization
primitives.verbatim_quote: **Incremental factor graph (GTSAM + ISAM2) for asynchronous localization.** Variables: camera poses X_i (priors from extrinsic calibration), ball 3D location L_t, 3D velocity V_t, 3D spin W_j (constant between bounces — spin only changes at ground contact).
primitives.assumptions: Camera poses known; ball motion modeled as piecewise constant spin between bounces; asynchronous detections update graph incrementally.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When spin estimation fails due to occlusion or lack of pose data.

layer2.mapping: Factor graph structure mirrors physical state evolution; each detection contributes a likelihood term to posterior belief over ball states.
layer2.telemetry: Localization accuracy (RMSE in meters) and convergence speed of ISAM2 iterations.

primitives.name: Temporal Convolutional Network Spin Prior
primitives.verbatim_quote: **TCN spin-prior network (§IV):** temporal convolutional network regressing ball spin from the 100-frame human-pose sequence (hip-centered, arm keypoints).
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'TCN': 'temporal convolutional network (architecture)', 'pose_sequence': '100-frame hip-centered arm keypoint sequence (normalized coordinates)', 'W_pred': 'predicted spin (rad/s)'}
primitives.assumptions: Human pose captures relevant kinematics; spin correlates with arm motion; pose data available at detection times.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When pose estimation fails or lacks sufficient arm articulation.

layer2.mapping: TCN maps pose features to spin parameters; trained end-to-end using self-distilled spin labels from factor graph inference.
layer2.telemetry: Correlation between predicted and fitted spin (R > 0.3) and reduction in early-flight prediction error.

reasoning_traces.think:
The core innovation lies in combining asynchronous multi-camera detection with a physics-informed factor graph that supports real-time inference. Each camera detection triggers an update to the graph via ISAM2, incorporating projection, motion, aerodynamic, and bounce factors. The spin prior is learned via a TCN from human pose data, addressing the unobservability of spin in early flight. This approach allows for accurate trajectory prediction even without synchronized camera frames. The system's strength resides in its modular design: the factor graph ensures consistency across views, while the TCN injects domain knowledge about spin generation. Failure modes include poor pose estimation, insufficient training data for the TCN, and inaccuracies in aerodynamic models at extreme spins or velocities. The model's reliance on self-distilled spin labels introduces potential circularity in training, which may limit generalizability beyond the training domain.
